title: Did the CIA test LSD on unsuspecting Americans?
summary: Josh and Chuck examine the CIA's LSD experiments in the 1950s, centered on MK Ultra and its subprojects. They cover the CIA's purchase of about forty hits of LSD from Sandoz Pharmaceuticals amid Cold War fears of Soviet mind control, the 149 MK Ultra subprojects, and the prisoner, addict and prostitute testing. The episode focuses on George Hunter White's New York apartment parties and San Francisco "Pad" safe house, the overseen role of Sidney Gottlieb, and the cases of Barbara Newsome and Dr. Frank Olson, whose death was ruled suicide but whose son later pursued murder claims. It ends with the claim that the CIA's involvement helped seed the 1960s counterculture through Ken Kesey and Stanley Owsley, followed by an off-topic McDonald's McDLT and McRib discussion and a sign-off.

entities.name: One Flew Over the Cuckoo's Nest

segments.title: Opening banter
segments.summary: Josh and Chuck open the show and introduce the topic of CIA LSD experiments on unsuspecting Americans, saying it is documented.

segments.title: Background: Cold War fears and Sandoz LSD
segments.summary: The hosts explain how LSD was a legitimate pharmaceutical developed by Albert Hofmann and made by Sandoz, and how Cold War fears of Soviet mind control led the CIA to buy about forty hits of the drug.

segments.title: MK Ultra and its subprojects
segments.summary: The CIA's MK Ultra program is described as having 149 subprojects, including magician sleight-of-hand poisoning, electroconvulsive therapy, radiation testing, and testing on prisoners and heroin addicts paid in heroin.

segments.title: Sidney Gottlieb and George Hunter White
segments.summary: The hosts profile Sidney Gottlieb, head of the CIA technical division, and George Hunter White, the agent who ran the LSD experiments and was known for amoral conduct and a background in an opium ring bust.

segments.title: New York parties and Barbara Newsome
segments.summary: White dosed friends at parties in his New York apartment, often serving spiked martinis. Barbara Newsome was dosed at one party, had a bad trip, and later suffered depression and repeated commitments.

segments.title: Frank Olson's death
segments.summary: Dr. Frank Olson, an Army scientist, was dosed at a party, had a severe reaction, and died after falling from a hotel window in New York eight days later. It was ruled suicide, but his son had the body exhumed and reported head trauma, and a former pimp said White ran the tests in New York.

segments.title: San Francisco Pad and Ike Feldman
segments.summary: White moved the operation to a San Francisco apartment called the Pad, which had a two-way mirror. He and recruit Ike Feldman picked up prostitutes, johns and drug dealers and dosed them with LSD.

segments.title: CIA link to the counterculture
segments.summary: The hosts argue the CIA indirectly helped spark the 1960s counterculture, citing Ken Kesey's participation in LSD trials, his Merry Pranksters, and his work with chemist Owsley, and mention Tom Wolfe's book.

segments.title: Sponsor read and McDonald's segue
segments.summary: A sponsor read for the reinvented 2012 camera, followed by a brief transition to a discussion of McDonald's menu items.

segments.title: McDonald's McRib and McDLT discussion and sign-off
segments.summary: Chuck and Josh discuss the McRib and the McDLT, plug a how stuff works article on McDonald's menu failures, and sign off.
